name: tests

on:
  push:            # every push to any branch (the USB gate must pass every time)
    branches: ["**"]   # not tag pushes: a release tag must not start a second run on its commit
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  change-scope:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      website_only: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.website_only }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Verify fail-closed change selection
        run: python tests/test_ci_change_scope.py
      - id: scope
        name: Select application test scope
        run: python scripts/ci_change_scope.py
  workspace-files:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [windows-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip
      - name: Install locked dependencies
        run: python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-release.lock
      - name: Required native workspace checks (no model or GUI)
        run: python scripts/check_workspace_files.py
  test:
    needs: change-scope
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # macOS: Apple Silicon (the Mac build targets M1 and newer)
        os: [windows-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip
      - name: Install
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          # The same packages the app needs (a hand-kept list here missed pypdf, U67-U71)
          python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-release.lock
      - name: USB portability (end to end, must pass every time)
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
        run: python -m pytest tests -m usb -v
      - name: Test
        if: needs.change-scope.outputs.website_only != 'true'
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
        run: python -m pytest tests -q --junitxml=test-results-${{ matrix.os }}.xml
      - name: Keep the machine-readable results (U102)
        if: always() && needs.change-scope.outputs.website_only != 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-results-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: test-results-${{ matrix.os }}.xml
  test-linux:
    needs: change-scope
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    # Linux (U101): the same suite on Ubuntu, so a Linux build has something to stand on. Not yet a
    # required check; it becomes one once it has passed on main for a while.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip
      - name: Qt's system libraries (offscreen, no display)
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libegl1 libgl1 libxkbcommon0 libfontconfig1 libdbus-1-3
      - name: Install
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-release.lock
      - name: USB portability (end to end)
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
        run: python -m pytest tests -m usb -v
      - name: Test
        if: needs.change-scope.outputs.website_only != 'true'
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
        run: python -m pytest tests -q --junitxml=test-results-ubuntu-latest.xml
      - name: Keep the machine-readable results (U102)
        if: always() && needs.change-scope.outputs.website_only != 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-results-ubuntu-latest
          path: test-results-ubuntu-latest.xml
  station-arm64:
    # Field Station preview (docs/FIELD-STATION-PLAN.md): the headless engine on Linux ARM64, the
    # Raspberry Pi 5's processor architecture, without the desktop's Qt toolkit. A GitHub ARM64 server is
    # not a Raspberry Pi: real hardware (sensors, Wi-Fi, USB, power) is validated separately.
    # Not a required check yet.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip
      - name: Install (engine only)
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install -r requirements-station.txt
      - name: Station and engine tests, with Qt blocked
        run: >
          python -c "import sys; sys.modules['PyQt6'] = None; import platform; print(platform.machine());
          import pytest; sys.exit(pytest.main(['-q', '--junitxml=test-results-station-arm64.xml',
          'tests/test_station_telemetry.py', 'tests/test_station_sessions.py', 'tests/test_station_server.py',
          'tests/test_station_storage.py', 'tests/test_fieldsync.py', 'tests/test_notebook_integrity_matrix.py',
          'tests/test_encryption_recovery.py', 'tests/test_calc_bench.py', 'tests/test_login_files.py',
          'tests/test_overconfidence.py', 'tests/test_team_drives.py']))"
      - name: Keep the machine-readable results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-results-station-arm64
          path: test-results-station-arm64.xml
  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - run: python -m pip install pip-audit==2.10.1 bandit==1.9.4
      - run: python -m pip_audit -r requirements-release.lock --no-deps --disable-pip
      - run: python -m bandit -r cursiv_engine launcher -lll -iii

name: mac-build

# Builds the macOS app (Apple Silicon) from a release tag: PyInstaller .app, a self-test of
# the built app, screenshots of its windows, an unsigned .dmg with its SHA-256. On a
# published release it attaches the .dmg to that release. Run by hand (Actions > mac-build >
# Run workflow) to build any branch or tag without publishing.

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: "Branch or tag to build"
        default: "main"
      upload:
        description: "Attach the .dmg to the release with this tag (tags only)"
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  checks: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest          # Apple Silicon
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      REF: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.ref }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.REF }}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip
      - name: Install
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-release.lock
      - name: Tests
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
        run: |
          python -m pytest tests -q
      - name: Require exact-source main release gates
        if: startsWith(env.REF, 'v')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if test -f scripts/prepare_release.py; then
            python -c "import subprocess,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');from prepare_release import require_ci;require_ci(subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip(),main_tip=False)"
          fi
      - name: Build Cursiv.app
        run: python -m PyInstaller --noconfirm --clean launcher/build.spec
      - name: Self-test the built app
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
        run: |
          ./dist/Cursiv.app/Contents/MacOS/Cursiv --selftest selftest.txt
          cat selftest.txt
      - name: Screenshots of the windows
        run: python scripts/mac_shots.py mac-shots || QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python scripts/mac_shots.py mac-shots
      - name: Make the .dmg
        run: |
          VERSION=$(python -c "import re;print(re.search(r'VERSION\s*=\s*\"([^\"]+)\"',open('cursiv_engine/core/selfknow.py').read()).group(1))")
          DMG="Cursiv-${VERSION}-mac-arm64.dmg"
          mkdir -p dmg
          cp -R dist/Cursiv.app dmg/
          ln -s /Applications dmg/Applications
          cp installer/mac/HOW-TO-OPEN.txt "dmg/How to open Cursiv.txt"
          hdiutil create -volname "Cursiv ${VERSION}" -srcfolder dmg -ov -format UDZO "$DMG"
          cp "$DMG" Cursiv-mac-latest.dmg          # a fixed name for the website's download button
          shasum -a 256 "$DMG" Cursiv-mac-latest.dmg | tee SHA256SUMS-mac.txt
          echo "DMG=$DMG" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Record build provenance
        run: python scripts/release_provenance.py provenance-mac.json "$DMG" Cursiv-mac-latest.dmg
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cursiv-mac
          path: |
            ${{ env.DMG }}
            SHA256SUMS-mac.txt
            selftest.txt
            provenance-mac.json
            mac-shots/
      - name: Attach to the release
        if: github.event_name == 'release' || (inputs.upload && startsWith(inputs.ref, 'v'))
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release view "$REF" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' | grep -Fxq 'owner-release.json'; then
            echo "Owner-signed assets are immutable; automatic replacement skipped."
            exit 0
          fi
          gh release upload "$REF" "$DMG" Cursiv-mac-latest.dmg SHA256SUMS-mac.txt provenance-mac.json

files.README.md:
# Cursiv Cursiv is a **free, open-source local AI assistant with tamper-evident notebooks**, offline document retrieval and portable Windows USB/SSD workspaces. Its SHA-256 record chain and linked corrections help preserve observation history and detect changes against a trusted record; they do not prove an observation was true. Built for researchers, technicians, independent workers and anyone keeping detailed records. Local language models run on your PC through Ollama. Cursiv is an application, not a new language model; model licenses are separate from its MIT license. Supported local features work offline after setup. [Local AI guide](https://cursiv.us/local-ai) · [Compare local AI tools](https://cursiv.us/compare) · [Documentation and evidence](https://cursiv.us/documentation)

[Mac build (early)](https://github.com/Cursiv-Local/Cursiv/releases/latest/download/Cursiv-mac-latest.dmg) · [Website](https://cursiv.us) · [Release notes](https://github.com/Cursiv-Local/Cursiv/releases/latest) ## What you can do - **Keep tamper-evident notes:** Record observations, photos and sample IDs. Verify the record chain and add corrections that preserve original entries. See [notebook integrity and its limits](docs/NOTEBOOK-INTEGRITY.md). - **Work with documents:** Import protocols and field guides, then ask questions about them with page references where available. - **Check calculations:** Convert units, work out distances and times, and calculate dilutions or statistics. - **Work with workspace files:** Create, read, append and search using plain requests inside a folder you authorize. - **Keep useful context:** Save selected facts and notes to find again later. Memory is selective, not a complete record of everything you say. - **Check answers:** See labels for supplied references, documents and calculations, alongside unchecked model replies. ## Get started **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.** Allow at least 8 GB RAM and roughly 6 GB of free space for an initial model; requirements vary by model. 1. Download and run the Windows installer above. 2. Create a local account. 3. Use Setup to install Ollama and download a model. Once it is ready, start chatting. The initial downloads need internet access. Type `offline on` to block Cursiv's internet connections afterward. Windows may show an unrecognized-publisher warning; Windows-trusted signing and Apple notarization are still pending. Read [how to verify a download](docs/OWNER-RELEASE-SIGNING.md) before continuing. Ask **“What can Cursiv do?”** for a short built-in guide with examples. To explore without using your own records, type `demo`. Type `demo off` to return to your data, or `help` to see the available commands. ## Phone and USB options - **[Phone notebook](https://cursiv.us/notebook):** Open it online once, then capture observations without signal. Export the file and import it into Cursiv. Export regularly—browser storage can be cleared. - **[Phone photo chat](https://cursiv.us/app):** A separate online page for questions about photos. It needs internet access. - **Portable Windows kit:** Choose **Make a Cursiv USB…** from the tray menu to include the app, Ollama runtime and selected model files. The host still needs compatible Windows hardware and drivers. See [what travels, privacy limits and physical-test boundaries](https://cursiv.us/portable-workspace). See [phone and portable setup](TECH.md#phone-and-portable-use) for instructions and limits. The Mac build is early; there is no Linux installer. ## Privacy and limits Local chat runs on your computer. Optional online services can receive the content sent to them when used or enabled. [Privacy details](PRIVACY.md). On a computer, conversations, memories and (from U98) the field notebook are always encrypted with a passphrase you choose at first start; a lost passphrase can't be recovered. A Cursiv USB drive stays readable by design (use drive encryption if it could be lost). The login only keeps people at your keyboard out; the passphrase is the real protection. [Coverage and recovery](TECH.md#conversation-and-memory-encryption-always-on). AI answers can be confidently wrong. Cursiv's checks catch some mistakes, not all of them. Verify important results. Cursiv is not certified for medical or safety-critical use, and its first-aid reference has not been professionally reviewed. ## Releases, evidence and development Latest release: **[U108](https://github.com/Cursiv-Local/Cursiv/releases/tag/v3.14-U108)**. See the [release notes](docs/RELEASE-U108.md) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). - [Tests and evidence](docs/CLAIM-EVIDENCE.md): what has been checked and what remains unverified. - [Help test Cursiv](https://cursiv.us/testers): send a clear report of what you tried and what happened. - [Contributor quick start](CONTRIBUTING.md): setup and checks. - [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [TECH.md](TECH.md): code layout, storage, builds and release details. Built by **Joshua Winkler**. Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

files.CONTRIBUTING.md:
# Quick start for contributors

Read these three files first:

1. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md): message flow and module ownership.
2. [TECH.md](TECH.md): data locations, setup, packaging and release safeguards.
3. [cursiv_engine/ui/chat_app.py](cursiv_engine/ui/chat_app.py): compatible chat
   facade; follow its calls into `chat/conversation.py` and `chat/completion.py`.

Looking for a specific thing? [docs/CODE-MAP.md](docs/CODE-MAP.md) lists every module in one
line, grouped by job, and a test keeps it complete. A first task to pick up:
[docs/GOOD-FIRST-ISSUES.md](docs/GOOD-FIRST-ISSUES.md).

## The one rule behind the code

Cursiv is for people who need to trust what it says. So anything that must be right (a saved record,
a calculation, a lookup, what Cursiv can do) is done by code and checked, and the AI model only words
it. If a change makes the model do more and the code check less, it's the wrong change. New behaviour
lands only with a test that would have caught the old failure, and model-facing changes with a
measured before/after (see `scripts/*_bench.py`).

## Run and check

Use a dedicated checkout and a Python 3.13 virtual environment. Install the exact
release dependencies with `python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-release.lock`.
Run `python launcher/main.py` from the repository root. Ollama is optional for
unit tests; real local-model use requires its separate installation and a model.

Before committing, run `python scripts/check_workspace_files.py`. This focused
workspace/language/release gate uses a disposable home and no GUI windows or model
calls. Then run the full suite below. Both gates must pass; do not push failing work.
GitHub main protection requires `workspace-files (windows-latest)`,
`workspace-files (macos-latest)`, both `test (...)` jobs and `security`, all from
GitHub Actions, with an up-to-date branch and no administrator bypass. Push a
feature branch and use a PR; the updated workflow must be present in that PR.
For releases use `scripts/prepare_release.py` after main CI passes; see TECH.

**The USB function must work every time.** `python -m pytest tests -m usb` runs the
USB gate (about 10 seconds): the whole make-drive → start from the drive → move it →
bring data back cycle (`tests/test_usb_end_to_end.py`) plus the sync, migration and
license tests. It runs before every commit once you enable the hook with
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, as its own step in the required `test` job on
every push and PR, and in `scripts/build_release.py`, which also starts the built
app from a USB layout and refuses to package it unless portable mode works.

Run `python -m pytest tests -q` in a disposable checkout/profile without personal
records, production keys or installed-app data. Fixtures redirect storage and
assert watched user data is unchanged. Qt tests use offscreen rendering and never
start Ollama automatically. Use synthetic data for encryption/migration tests;
never enable a test vault on someone else's records.

Website-only checks: `node cloudflare/publish.mjs --build-only`, then run the
`cloudflare/tests/*.test.mjs` files with Node's test runner. On PowerShell pass the
expanded filenames, for example `node --test (Get-ChildItem cloudflare/tests -Filter '*.test.mjs').FullName`.
Build-only does not deploy. The existing PyInstaller specification and
`scripts/build_release.py` define packaging; package renames must update both.

## Boundaries to preserve

- Launcher owns widgets, desktop lifecycle and entry points. Engine owns policy,
  calculations, providers, receipts, notebook and memory backends. See the flagged
  legacy ownership exceptions in ARCHITECTURE rather than copying their design.
- Native results establish execution. Model text never authorizes a tool or proves
  a save. Keep read-only reads, talk-only blocks and memory restrictions tested.
- Do not change the local-first cascade or bypass `core/netgate.py`.
- Notebook chains are append-only; corrections are new entries. Keep signing,
  sample-ID collision, imports and portable path tests intact.
- Protected data writes use the explicit storage boundary. Never add plaintext
  temporary copies, backups, caches or logging of passphrases/messages around it.
- Keep release private keys out of the repository, OneDrive and CI. Existing owner
  signatures and immutable release evidence must remain verifiable.

## Keep documentation reviewable

Update the changelog, relevant architecture/privacy guidance and existing evidence
index with behavior changes. Link README claims to [CLAIM-EVIDENCE](docs/CLAIM-EVIDENCE.md).
Record actual commands/results and distinguish source tests, model benchmarks,
packaged checks and physical testing. Historical results retain their release/model
labels. Prefer updating these documents over adding a new micro-repair report.

Make focused commits; do not include local data, generated reports, signing keys,
installers or unrelated user work. Pushes, releases and deployment require the
owner's current authorization.
